conflicts.description: The production manual's complete driver chart (PDF 44 / printed 40) calls every flasher circuit Bulb #89. Its detailed eight-branch wiring drawing (PDF 88 / printed 84) instead specifies three #89 plus one #906 on 1R/3R/5R/6R/8R and two of each on 4R. The drawing retains older location wording, including a drop-target 1R lamp absent from the production location drawing and photographs, so its mixed bulb populations cannot silently override the production chart. Both sources agree on four sockets per circuit, and 2R/7R agree on all #89. The generic parts totals contain an inherited other-game footnote and do not settle per-circuit populations. Pinned PinMAME uniformly models 25-32 as #89 brightness, which is not physical fitment evidence. Resolution path: an owner or technician can supply socket-and-bulb close-ups, traced by harness to circuits 1R/3R/4R/5R/6R/8R on an unrestored production Baywatch, or a later production wiring revision can assign those exact socket populations. Wide playfield photos and ROM traces cannot identify every bulb base or settle this disagreement.

The cabinet wiring drawing (PDF 86 / printed 82) explicitly draws STEP and FOR/REV as normally-open contacts. Bulletin 74 requires both buttons to be momentary: remove the silver C-shaped latching wire form from the early green switch. des112 uses DE_COMPORTS2 and the ROM uses Enter and Select in Portals; the older diagnostics prose still describes FORWARD/REVERSE navigation. Electrical contact rest state and mechanical latching are separate facts.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP6364 = FLIP_SWNO(63,64) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. DE2.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP6364 = FLIP_SWNO(63,64) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 64 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 64: a host write to 64 is overwritten on the next update. The table calls de2.vbs vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp, whose swLRFlip is 82. Both upper and lower right flippers have cabinet switch wiring in the game's SSFB diagram; the upper pair additionally accept CPU output 13.

mechanisms.behavior: Five balls occupy mechanical microswitch positions 10 (left) through 14 (right). Output 1 releases the lock-ball cam toward the opto-monitored up-kicker 15; output 2 lifts that ball to shooter lane 16. Output 3 then launches it onto the elevated shooter wire ramp. The script initializes bsTrough with switches 14,13,12,11,10 and five balls, then a separate bsTroughUp saucer at 15. TroughLock transfers one ball; bsTroughUpSolOut ejects the up-kicker. The 250ms table delay and kick strength are table tuning, not physical specifications.
mechanisms.label: Five-ball trough and two-stage serve

mechanisms.behavior: The cabinet launch button 50 requests a shot. Output 3 fires Plunger1 at the lower-right shooter entrance (switch 16), feeding the elevated shooter wire ramp toward the top SPF lanes. This is independent of the upper mid-right kicker 4.
mechanisms.label: Lower automatic launch

mechanisms.behavior: Output 4 fires UpBLaunch at the mid-right side, with ball-presence rollover 47, sending a ball through the upper launch path. Both script plungers fire rearward along their own guides; do not treat output 4 as a second winding or direction of output 3.
mechanisms.label: Upper ball launch / Kick Big

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer at rear-left switch 44 captures the ball; output 5 ejects it up to its wire return. bsUpVUK is distinct from both the under-apron Super VUK and the left Shark Super Scoop.
mechanisms.label: Rear upper VUK

mechanisms.behavior: Balls entering the under-playfield ramp at 55 travel to the lower front-left Super VUK 46 under the arch. Output 6 ejects them back to play through the subway exit. The table uses a separate bsLowSVuk saucer at 46.
mechanisms.label: Under-playfield return and lower Super VUK

mechanisms.behavior: The left mid-playfield scoop 56 receives Shark shots and holds a ball until output 7 ejects it. bsSSScoop uses its own ball stack. It is not the lower under-arch VUK.
mechanisms.label: Shark Super Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: Completing the three-drop bank lights the lock trapdoor on the left metal ramp. Output 12 opens the physical door to divert a ball into the under-playfield ramp (55), which feeds lower VUK 46; with the door closed, the ramp continues toward exit 26. The tower's lamps 33/34/35 indicate collected locks; there are no three dedicated tower-ball sensors. The script opens Botola and swaps RampLG collision helpers while 12 is on.
mechanisms.label: Tower ramp lock trapdoor

mechanisms.behavior: Output 9 opens UpperGate; off returns it. The factory overview places this gate under the left ramp near the top rollovers. Rollover scoring switches are route sensors, not gate-limit feedback.
mechanisms.label: Upper one-way control gate

mechanisms.behavior: Output 14 opens LowerGate at the mid-right upper launch/Shark Fin route; off returns it. The manual puts the mini-coil under the butyrate. Switches 47 and 54 detect balls along the route, not a measured gate position.
mechanisms.label: Lower one-way control gate

mechanisms.behavior: Rollover 54 lies before the upper-right Shark Fin. When Shark Flips is lit the ROM times output 13 to shoot toward the Shark Super Scoop. The manual's Shark Fin test and Adjustment 50 tune this timing. Q26 drives both upper flipper enables through isolation diodes; the script AutoFlipper rotates both upper bats. Each upper flipper also has its side's cabinet-button path, shown as N.O. on the SSFB schematic. No physical upper EOS switches are fitted.
mechanisms.label: Shark Flips automatic upper pair

mechanisms.behavior: Targets 22/23/24 latch down independently, ordered top/middle/bottom. Output 16 resets the whole bank through cdtBank.DropSol_On. Completing the bank lights a tower lock; release the three contacts when the physical bank rises.
mechanisms.label: Three-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Left, bottom and right switches 41/42/43 correspond to special-solenoid outputs 17/18/19. The script's Hit callbacks pulse the switches; PinMAME's DMD ROM drives the PIA special-solenoid lines. No alpha-game sequential-SP assumption is used.
mechanisms.label: Three turbo bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left 61 and right 62 trigger their respective kickers 20 and 21. The table's collision flippers are alternative simulation geometry; they are not additional physical flipper assemblies.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: When enabled by the ROM, left outlane switch 57 causes output 22 to kick the ball back up that lane. Completing the two stand-up targets 9/53 relights it. LaserKick.FireSpeed randomness in the table is tuning, not a measured factory value.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane Laser Kick

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower flippers and two upper flippers are fitted. Cabinet buttons 82/84 are copied to ROM matrix 64/63. PinMAME fabricates 45/46 and 47/48 together, so use one state per side and do not create independent power/hold actuators. The script's right callback moves RightFlipper and RightFlipper1, and its left callback moves LeftFlipper and LeftFlipper1. The physical upper pair also accepts CPU 13 through SSFB isolation diodes, represented by mech.shark-flips. The lower EOS power-cutoff contacts are board-local; no host-driven EOS input is exposed.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet-controlled flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 pulses the cabinet-mounted 23-800 knocker. It has no ball-route sensor and no playfield placement.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet knocker

mechanisms.behavior: PPB K1 relay 10 selects alternate coil/flasher loads for drives 1-8 and 25-32. G.I. relay 11 independently switches the illumination supply; the table's inverted local lamp 200 animates these bulbs without adding another public output. Socket counts belong to the individual lighting circuits, not these relay mechanisms.
mechanisms.label: PPB bank selection and G.I. control

physical.notes: Printed circuit 1L. The whole driver table, including merged and unused cells, is retained in coils.md. 25-1240 lock-ball cam releases one of five trough balls toward the separate up-kicker; no physical lock-cam object exists in the retained table.
Printed circuit 2L. The whole driver table, including merged and unused cells, is retained in coils.md.
